target_customer: Real estate private equity, developers and brokers who need ownership, pricing, zoning and operating data
problem: Real estate data is fragmented across web sources, emails and calls, and incumbent databases are costly.

founders.name: Clarence Chen
founders.background_notes: No background on YC page. A search snippet mentions a prior education company exit, unverified.

founders.name: Michael Dalva
education: CS and AI, Stanford (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Researched hardware fault resilience in ML pipelines and wrote code for satellites per YC page.

founders.name: Ashwin Sriram
founders.background_notes: Linux security experience per YC page.

competitors.name: CoStar
competitors.what: Incumbent commercial real estate database, costly per month

competitors.name: Reonomy
competitors.what: CRE property data platform, acquired by Altus Group in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Crawling, entity resolution and AI calling and emailing to fill data gaps is standard but laborious engineering for a four person team.

defensibility.rationale: A compounding proprietary dataset can deepen over time, but coverage and accuracy are unproven per press.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Travo found as of 2026-11.

market_need_then: Press describes CoStar as expensive for smaller firms, a gap Travo targets with AI aggregation. The launch post says the team first tried real estate private equity agents and decided the underlying data was the missing piece.

branding.domain_note: Uses travoai.com, not travo.com; an unrelated TRAVO, Inc. (business travel) exists with dead 2015 trademarks.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand; the home page is only a title and tagline.

pivots.from: Agents for real estate private equity workflows
pivots.why: Founders concluded they needed better underlying data, per the YC launch post (date approximate).

outcome_analysis: Travo is a Winter 2026 YC company that pivoted from private equity workflow agents to a real estate data platform. No shutdown or acquisition was found as of November 2026. Funding is unknown and the field is crowded with incumbents, so its outcome is open.
notes: No verified funding found; Crunchbase and CB Insights entries match different companies. The launch post (via the YC page fetch) calls the founders Stanford CS dropouts but a search found no corroboration.
